name: The One-Unit Central-Square Profile Cannot Be Shielded
statement: Under the one-unit opposite-wing hypotheses, a cornerless ample two-layer family has three pairwise disjoint acquired direction pairs. In particular, the exceptional central-square support graph $K_{2,2}$ cannot occur.
proof: Assume the central-square alternative and fix either wing. Its active slice is the singleton $\{c\}$, its uncounted vertex $v$ is opposite $c$ in the central square, and the square directions $z_1,z_2$ are passive attachment directions. Every exclusive concept has the passive word of $c$, so $v$ is at passive distance two from that word. The two pendant paths attach at the other antipodal pair of the square, making $v$ a corner of the overlap $B$. This contradicts passive radius-one shielding in a cornerless family.
